facts.fact: Media Rights Agenda reports that the Freedom of Information Act, 2011 is in force and gives a right of access to information held by public bodies, as shown by a Federal High Court judgment enforcing it in 2026; the year 2011 is the Act's year as named in the report.

A Federal High Court in Lagos (Justice Aneke) ruled on 24 February 2026, in a suit on a journalist's October 2020 request, that the Nigeria Shippers Council breached the Freedom of Information Act and ordered it to disclose the information or give reasons for withholding it.

The Federal High Court, Abuja, applies the Freedom of Information Act, 2011 as the specific, operative access to information legislation, taking precedence over the Petroleum Industry Act where they conflict.

In suit FHC/ABJ/CS/1631/2023 the Federal High Court, Abuja, held NNPCL a public institution under the FOI Act and ordered it by mandamus to supply the information HEDA Resources Centre had requested on a $3 billion crude-for-cash loan.

This document is the text of the Freedom of Information Act, 2011, passed by both Houses on 24 May 2011 and assented to by President Jonathan on 28 May 2011; it establishes a right of any person to request information held by public institutions.
The Global Data Barometer report lists freedom of information legislation among the transparency reforms Nigeria has adopted over the past two decades.
Pollicy says Nigeria's Freedom of Information Act, enacted in 2011, grants citizens access to public records.

note: The document covers an OC4IDS infrastructure data portal and a state disclosure mandate; it states nothing about an access to information law.

facts.fact: Media Rights Agenda reports the Freedom of Information Act is being implemented, with Section 29 requiring public institutions to report annually to the Attorney-General.

The Attorney-General's 2025 implementation report to the National Assembly, submitted 24 March 2026, gives requests received by institutions (for example NBC 40, CBN 29, NTA 17) from 108 reporting institutions, with 180 listed as defaulters.
The Guardian reports the Federal High Court applying the Freedom of Information Act's duties and exemptions to the NDDC forensic audit report.
The Guardian reports Justice Olotu ordering the President to publish the NDDC forensic audit report and the names of those indicted, in an FOI suit brought by SERAP.
Punch reports the Court of Appeal holding that the Freedom of Information Act imposes a legal duty of disclosure on the Central Bank.
Punch reports the Court of Appeal dismissed the CBN's appeal and upheld the order to disclose 2016-2020 Hajj forex subsidy details requested by HEDA under the FOI Act.

Punch reports the Federal High Court in Abuja held on 15 July 2025 that the National Population Commission's refusal of a records request breached rights under Sections 1, 2 and 4 of the FOI Act, 2011.

Punch reports Justice H.J. Yilwa of the Federal High Court ordered the National Population Commission on 15 July 2025 to release procurement records requested by NEFGAD under the Freedom of Information Act.

The Guardian reports the Freedom of Information Act was assented to in 2011 and is applied to public institutions, with the Justice Ministry's FoI unit confirming 91 of about 800 institutions complied in 2023.

note: No dated decision or request figures by an oversight body; court fine on the CBN is undated.

facts.fact: The Federal High Court in Abuja held that the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs violated the Freedom of Information Act, 2011, by refusing a request for information, so the Act is in force.

Justice Binta Nyako of the Federal High Court ordered the Ministry to release the Ondo cash-transfer beneficiary list within seven days and awarded N2m damages for breaching the applicant's right under the FOI Act.

The communique of the Abuja stakeholders' meeting (IPC, PLAC, YIAGA Africa) treats the Freedom of Information Act as the law in force, with 14 years of implementation, and says a Supreme Court judgment of 11 April 2025 confirmed it applies to state-level public institutions.
